overall_summary: Space anomalies and bizarre animal survival mechanisms are driving the highest engagement and views, while generic cognitive psychology facts are consistently underperforming.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Largest Ocean in Space Will Mind-Blow You!' (460 views) and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) are the channel's top performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more shorts that translate abstract space concepts into tangible, surprising sensory experiences (smell, taste, touch).

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre animal survival and evolutionary paradoxes
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) show high relative engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on extreme biological adaptations and historical-biological timeline anomalies that challenge common sense.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic cognitive psychology and brain function facts
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) failed to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from abstract brain mechanisms unless they can be framed with a highly personal, immediate self-test hook.

next_video.concept: The Planet of Burning Ice (Gliese 436 b)
next_video.opening_direction: Show a visual of ice engulfed in roaring flames and ask: 'How can ice exist at 800 degrees Fahrenheit without melting?'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's gravity is so incredibly immense that it compresses water molecules into solid ice, despite the scorching temperatures.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful space category and uses a strong sensory contradiction hook, similar to the top-performing space ocean and space smell videos.

experiment: A/B test identical scripts with two different visual styles: one using realistic 3D space renders and another using stylized, high-contrast AI-generated animations to see which holds viewer retention better in the first 3 seconds.
